one_line_description.value: Stripe lets businesses accept payments online, collect payments with invoices, and accept payments in person.
one_line_description.quote: ## Payments - Accept payments online - Collect payments with invoices - Accept payments in-person

has_public_api.quote: The Stripe API is organized around REST. Our API has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts form-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.

api_type.quote: The Stripe API is organized around REST.

api_breadth.value: REST, resource-oriented API; object-level operations only, no bulk updates.
api_breadth.quote: The Stripe API doesn’t support bulk updates. You can work on only one object per request.

auth_methods.quote: Provide your API key as the basic auth username value. If you need to authenticate using bearer auth (for example, for a cross-origin request), use `-H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_...sk_test_..."` instead of `-u sk_test_...sk_test_...`.

access_model.quote: run `stripe sandbox create --help` to provision an anonymous Stripe sandbox with working API keys. It doesn’t require account registration.

access_notes.value: Anonymous Stripe sandbox with working API keys can be provisioned via the Stripe CLI without account registration.
access_notes.quote: run `stripe sandbox create --help` to provision an anonymous Stripe sandbox with working API keys. It doesn’t require account registration.

official_mcp_server.quote: Follow your client’s MCP setup instructions and use `https://mcp.stripe.com` as the server URL.

rate_limits.value: Live mode: 100 requests/sec global; sandbox: 25 requests/sec global; individual endpoints: 25 requests/sec.
rate_limits.quote: | Global API rate limit | Live mode: 100 requests per second Sandbox: 25 requests per second | | Individual API endpoints (unless otherwise noted) | 25 requests per second |

webhooks.quote: Handle delivery failures, signature errors, and event-generation failures for your webhook endpoints.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: A sandbox is an isolated test environment.

sdk_languages.quote: ### Client libraries - Ruby - Python - PHP - Java - Node.js - Go - .NET

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: The Stripe API differs for every account as Stripe releases new versions and tailors functionality.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: The Stripe API differs for every account as we release new versions and tailor functionality.

verdict_reason: Stripe publishes a public REST API reference with official SDKs and documents API-key, HTTP Basic, and Bearer authentication. Its docs also state that a Stripe CLI command can provision an anonymous sandbox with working API keys without account registration. Rate limits, webhooks, sandboxes, and an official MCP server are documented, so access is self-serve and the API is broad enough to build against.
open_questions: The dedicated Stripe API OAuth 2.0 authentication page appeared only in search snippets, not in SOURCES; auth_methods therefore omits oauth2 and oauth_scopes_documented is not_found.
No full API versioning/deprecation or sunset-policy page is in SOURCES; only the statement that the API differs by account as new versions are released.
No endpoint/resource count is available in SOURCES, so api_breadth is qualitative.
No community MCP servers were found in the supplied GitHub/MCP-registry checks (both returned no results).
Production/live-mode access requirements are not fully documented in the supplied sources; access_model reflects anonymous sandbox access for development/testing.
